intro: Hi! I'm the AI Upscaler support assistant. I answer from every support topic we've ever handled (each with a step-by-step guide), and I can search all GitHub issues live. Ask about install errors, GPU not used, Docker/NAS setup, API tokens, models, and more. You can ask in English or German.

entries.title: Plugin won't install / checksum mismatch
entries.answer:
Jellyfin checks the plugin ZIP's MD5 against the repo manifest and rejects any mismatch. A checksum error on a current version almost always means a **stale cached repo**. Step by step:
1. Use the official repo URL: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kuschel-code/JellyfinUpscalerPlugin/main/repository-jellyfin.json`
2. Dashboard → Plugins → **Repositories** → remove the AI Upscaler repo.
3. Re-add the repository (same URL).
4. **Restart Jellyfin** (this clears the cached manifest).
5. Catalog → AI Upscaler → install the **latest version** shown.
6. Still failing? Paste the exact error + your Jellyfin version.

entries.title: "No newer version available" / can't update
entries.answer:
Jellyfin caches the plugin catalog. Step by step:
1. Dashboard → Plugins → **Repositories**.
2. Remove the AI Upscaler repository.
3. Re-add it (URL: `.../main/repository-jellyfin.json`).
4. **Restart Jellyfin**.
5. Hard-refresh the dashboard (Ctrl+F5).
6. Catalog now shows the latest release.

If you added the repository long ago with the `.../main/manifest.json` URL: that feed briefly lagged behind in mid-2026 (issue #74) — it is synced again, so a refresh now shows the latest version on any of the repo URLs.

entries.title: Plugin "Not Supported" / incompatible with my Jellyfin
entries.answer:
Match the plugin to your Jellyfin server.
1. v1.8.3.32 is a Jellyfin 12 / .NET 10 release with minimum ABI 12.0.0.0. Do not install it on 10.11.
2. v1.8.3.31 is the published 10.11.8-ABI build.
3. Install the complete six-file release ZIP and restart Jellyfin.
4. If the plugin is disabled, inspect the server log for ABI, missing assembly or initialization errors.

entries.title: Unable to connect to the Docker AI service
entries.answer:
The plugin reaches the Docker container over HTTP. Step by step:
1. Confirm the container is **running**.
2. Confirm port **5000** is published (`-p 5000:5000`).
3. In a browser open `http://YOUR-SERVER-IP:5000/health` → expect `{"status":"healthy"}`.
4. In the plugin set **AI Service URL** = `http://YOUR-SERVER-IP:5000` (use the LAN IP, not `localhost`, if Jellyfin runs in its own container).
5. Make sure no firewall / reverse proxy blocks port 5000.
6. Click **Test Connection** in the plugin config.

entries.title: GPU detected but inference runs on CPU (slow)
entries.answer:
If `/gpu-verify` shows `AzureExecutionProvider`, you're on the wrong/old image (plain onnxruntime, no GPU provider). Step by step:
1. Choose the right image: `docker7-intel` / `docker7-amd` / `docker7` (NVIDIA).
2. Force a fresh pull:
```
docker compose pull
docker compose up -d --force-recreate
```
3. Pass the GPU device: `--gpus all` (NVIDIA), `/dev/dri` (Intel/AMD Linux), or `/dev/dxg` (WSL2).
4. On native Linux also add `group_add: render`.
5. Re-check `http://IP:5000/gpu-verify` → `active_providers` should list a non-CPU provider.
(v1.7.8 also fixed a display bug where `using_gpu:false` showed even with OpenVINO active — trust `active_providers`.)

entries.title: Intel Arc / iGPU on Windows or WSL2 not used
entries.answer:
Step by step for Intel Arc / iGPU on Windows/WSL2:
1. Use the **`docker7-intel`** image (it bundles `onnxruntime-openvino`).
2. Pass **`/dev/dxg`** (NOT `/dev/dri/renderD128`) and mount `/usr/lib/wsl`.
3. Force a fresh image: `docker compose pull` (plain `up` reuses the cached old one).
4. `docker compose up -d --force-recreate`.
5. Check `http://IP:5000/gpu-verify` → should show `OpenVINOExecutionProvider`.
6. For full-length files use **batch** mode — live 4x HD is too heavy for an A380.

entries.title: ONNX error / "Reshape" / wrong input type / FP16 crash
entries.answer:
Both ONNX warmup errors are fixed. Step by step:
1. Update to the **latest** Docker images: `docker compose pull && docker compose up -d --force-recreate`.
2. The FP16-on-FP32 crash (`INVALID_ARGUMENT`) was fixed in v1.7.4 — FP16 is only used when the loaded model agrees.
3. The `Reshape` warmup error on `realesrgan-x4-256` was fixed in v1.7.8 — the benchmark now reads the model's real input shape.
4. Restart the container and retry the model.

entries.title: Set the API token / "not configured" / 401 Unauthorized
keywords: where do i set the token
entries.answer:
The API token is a **shared secret you choose** that gates the Docker AI service so only your plugin can use it. For the env secret there's **no "generate" button** — you set the **same value in two places** (or pick the no-auth path); the plugin's *API Tokens* tab can additionally mint named tokens (see below).

**Home/LAN (simplest)** — turn auth off:
1. Set `API_TOKEN=disable` on the container.
2. Restart the container. The "not configured" message is gone and model downloads work.

**Secure it instead** — same secret in both places:
1. On the Docker container set `API_TOKEN=your-secret` (docker-compose: `environment:` → `- API_TOKEN=your-secret`).
2. In the plugin: **Settings → AI Service API Token** — paste the identical value, then Save.
3. Restart the container. If the two differ, the service returns **401/403**.
4. Verify: open `http://YOUR-IP:5000/status` → expect `api_token_configured: true` and `auth_enabled: true`.

**Named / expiring tokens (v1.8+)**: the plugin's **API Tokens** tab (Jellyfin admin) also mints named tokens with an optional expiry (30 days / 90 days / 1 year / never). Each is shown once, stored only as a hash, and revocable individually; the `API_TOKEN` env value stays valid as a non-revocable bootstrap.
Full walkthrough: the **API** page on the project website.

entries.title: Non-admin users can't use the plugin (models won't load)
entries.answer:
Fixed in **v1.7.5** (31 endpoints downgraded from admin-only to authenticated-user). Step by step:
1. Update the plugin to the **latest version**.
2. Restart Jellyfin.
3. Have the non-admin user reload the player — they can now load/use models.

entries.title: 4:3 video is stretched to fill the screen
entries.answer:
Fixed in **v1.7.5** (`object-fit: contain` on the real-time overlay). Step by step:
1. Update the plugin to the **latest version**.
2. Restart Jellyfin.
3. Reload the video player — 4:3 sources now letterbox correctly instead of stretching.

entries.title: AMD GPU support (ROCm / Vulkan)
entries.answer:
Two AMD paths. **ROCm (`docker7-amd`)** — step by step:
1. Use the `docker7-amd` image (v1.7.8 fixed it actually using the GPU; earlier it ran on CPU).
2. Pass `/dev/kfd` **and** `/dev/dri`, plus `--group-add video`.
3. Check `/gpu-verify` → `ROCMExecutionProvider`.

**Vulkan (`docker7-vulkan`, best for older cards)** — step by step:
1. Use the `docker7-vulkan` image.
2. Pass `/dev/dri`.
3. ncnn-Vulkan runs on most AMD/Intel GPUs.

entries.title: NVIDIA / RTX error, crash, or provider load failure
entries.answer:
Step by step for NVIDIA:
1. Use the **`docker7`** (NVIDIA) image.
2. Install the NVIDIA Container Toolkit on the host.
3. Run with `--gpus all` (or `runtime: nvidia` in compose).
4. Verify GPU passthrough: `docker exec <container> nvidia-smi` must succeed.
5. If you saw `INVALID_ARGUMENT` or a `libonnxruntime_providers` load error, update to the **latest version** (v1.7.8 brought FP16 + provider fixes) and re-pull.
6. Check `/gpu-verify` → `CUDAExecutionProvider` / `TensorrtExecutionProvider`.

entries.title: Real-time stays on Standby: "Video color metadata unavailable"
entries.answer:
**Fixed in v1.8.3.34.** v1.8.3.31–v1.8.3.33 refused real-time upscaling for *every* video in the Jellyfin web client with "Video color metadata unavailable; realtime processing cannot be validated", and the menu stayed on **Standby**. The player looked for the playing item in the page address, which Jellyfin 10.9 and later no longer contains. The AI service is not the cause: if its log ends with `Uvicorn running on http://0.0.0.0:5000`, it is fine.
1. Update the plugin to **v1.8.3.34** (Dashboard → Plugins → Catalog), restart Jellyfin, then reload the browser tab (Ctrl+F5) so the new player script loads.
2. Play the video again. If the message stays, run **⋮ → Refresh metadata** on the item once: a file Jellyfin has not scanned yet has no colour information to check.
3. Still refused? Open an issue and include the browser console lines that start with `AI Upscaler`.

v1.8.3.31, the version for Jellyfin 10.11, has the same defect.

entries.title: Real-time keeps falling back to WebGL / poor playback
entries.answer:
Real-time server upscaling needs a GPU that keeps up with the video's frame rate. Step by step:
1. Let **Auto** decide: it only picks Server AI when the benchmark reaches 80 % of the video's frame rate, otherwise it runs Lanczos in your browser.
2. Don't expect live 4x on HD video; most GPUs can't sustain it (even an Arc A380).
3. For the best quality, run a **scheduled task** (batch) once, then play the resulting `<name>_upscaled` file normally.
4. For live playback keep it light: a fast model (`realesr-general-x4v3`, `span-x2`) and/or 2x.

**v1.8.3.33** switches to Lanczos again when frames arrive at under half the video's frame rate for 5 s. v1.8.3.31–v1.8.3.32 did not; there, change the mode in the AI Upscaler menu (**Realtime** tab).

entries.title: Batch upscale job stuck at 95% / where are the files?
entries.answer:
95% is the final **re-mux** stage. Step by step to diagnose:
1. The finished file is `<name>_upscaled.<ext>` next to the source; a failed partial is auto-deleted (so nothing's left to find).
2. Intermediate frames live in the container's `/tmp` (not host-visible).
3. While it's stuck, run `docker logs --tail 80 <container>` and `docker exec <container> df -h /tmp`.
4. If `/tmp` is ~100% full, add a volume in compose: `- ai-tmp:/tmp`.
5. Recreate the container and re-run the job.

entries.title: Which model should I use?
entries.answer:
Pick by goal. Step by step:
1. **Fast / low-VRAM:** `realesr-general-x4v3` (~5MB), `lsdir-compact-v2-x4`, `spanx2-ch48`.
2. **Best quality:** `nomos2-dat2-x4`, `drct-l-x4`, `nomos8k-hat-l-x4` (heavy — poster/backdrop).
3. **Compressed / streaming sources:** `realwebphoto-v4-dat2-x4`.
4. **Anime:** `real-cugan-x4`, `apisr-anime-x2`.
5. Download it from the `http://IP:5000` dashboard, then select it in the player overlay or set `DEFAULT_MODEL`.

entries.title: Setup on ZimaOS / CasaOS / Synology / TrueNAS / Unraid
entries.answer:
Deploy with docker compose. Step by step:
1. In your NAS app manager, add a custom app / import a Docker Compose:
```
services:
  ai-upscaler:
    image: kuscheltier/jellyfin-ai-upscaler:docker7-cpu
    ports: ["5000:5000"]
    environment: ["API_TOKEN=disable"]
    volumes: ["ai-models:/app/models"]
    restart: unless-stopped
volumes:
  ai-models:
```
2. Intel iGPU? Use `docker7-intel` and add `devices: ["/dev/dri:/dev/dri"]`.
3. Start it, open `http://NAS-IP:5000` to confirm it's up.
4. In the plugin set **AI Service URL** = `http://NAS-IP:5000`.
5. Download a model. (TrueNAS: a ready compose is in `docker-ai-service/truenas/`.)

entries.title: Scan only specific libraries (not everything)
entries.answer:
Implemented in v1.6.1.14+. Step by step:
1. Update to the **latest version** (feature exists since v1.6.1.14).
2. Dashboard → Plugins → AI Upscaler → **Settings** tab.
3. In the **library picker**, tick the libraries you want scanned.
4. Save. (Leave all unticked = scan everything, the default.)

entries.title: Old docker5 / docker6 tag missing
entries.answer:
The old tag families (`docker4/5/6/6.1`) are retired. Step by step:
1. In your compose/run, change the image tag to **`docker7-<backend>`** (e.g. `docker7-intel`), or pin a specific version tag **`:vX.Y.Z-<backend>`**.
2. `docker compose pull`.
3. `docker compose up -d`.

entries.title: Getting started / is the plugin usable?
entries.answer:
From zero. Step by step:
1. Deploy the **Docker AI service** (compose — see the NAS/setup topic).
2. Open `http://server:5000` → confirm the dashboard loads and **download a model**.
3. In Jellyfin, install the plugin from the repo.
4. Plugin config → **AI Service URL** = `http://server:5000` → Save.
5. Use it: **batch** mode (nightly scheduled task) upscales your library; **real-time** mode enhances during playback.
6. See the Installation and Configuration pages for details.

entries.title: Plugin won't enable / "Failed to load assembly" / disappears (tombstoned)
entries.answer:
A missing runtime DLL or incompatible server ABI can prevent startup.
1. Install the official ZIP with JellyfinUpscalerPlugin.dll, FFMpegCore.dll, CliWrap.dll, Instances.dll, SixLabors.ImageSharp.dll and meta.json.
2. From source, run dotnet publish and Scripts/package-plugin.py; do not ship test binaries, PDBs, Scripts or deps.json.
3. Use ABI 12.0.0.0 for the 1.8.3.32 release; 1.8.3.31 uses ABI 10.11.8.0.
4. Re-enable through the admin dashboard or POST /Plugins/{id}/{version}/Enable using Authorization: MediaBrowser Token="<admin token>". Never share that token.
5. Restart Jellyfin and inspect the plugin load log.

entries.title: Plugin settings won't save / changes don't apply
entries.answer:
An old bug where saving dropped fields (Docker URL/IP/port reset to defaults), **fixed in v1.6.1.14**. Step by step:
1. Update the plugin to the **latest version**.
2. Restart Jellyfin.
3. Dashboard → Plugins → AI Upscaler → re-enter your settings.
4. Click **Save**.
5. If a field still resets on the latest version, open an issue naming that field.

entries.title: No Settings / config page after installing
entries.answer:
Step by step:
1. The config lives at **Dashboard → Plugins → AI Upscaler** (click the plugin name).
2. No entry there? The plugin didn't load — see the "Plugin won't enable" topic (install the official ZIP, restart Jellyfin).
3. Update to the **latest version** and restart Jellyfin.
4. Hard-refresh the browser (Ctrl+F5).

entries.title: FFmpeg/ffprobe crash — "Cannot start process / file name not provided"
keywords: file name has not been provided
entries.answer:
An old ffmpeg cold-start bug (paths captured before Jellyfin resolved them), **fixed in v1.6.1.21**. Step by step:
1. Update to the **latest version**.
2. Dashboard → Playback → confirm Jellyfin's bundled FFmpeg is detected.
3. Restart Jellyfin.
4. Re-run the scheduled task — paths are now late-resolved on every entry point.

entries.title: Run the Setup Doctor (one-shot self-diagnosis)
entries.answer:
v1.7.9 adds a one-shot Setup Doctor that inspects YOUR running AI service and tells you exactly what to fix. Step by step:
1. Open http://YOUR-SERVER-IP:5000/doctor in a browser (or run: curl http://IP:5000/doctor | jq). The Docker dashboard also has a 'Setup Check' button on the Hardware tab.
2. Read the rows top to bottom - each is green (ok) / amber (warn) / red (fail) with a copy-paste fix.
3. backend: which image/GPU was detected (info only).
4. gpu_provider_active: red means you are on CPU - pull the matching docker7-<nvidia|amd|intel> image and pass the GPU device.
5. device_passthrough: red prints the exact line for your backend (--gpus all, or /dev/dri, or WSL2 /dev/dxg + group_add).
6. onnx_provider_pkg: red means the wrong onnxruntime build (a plain onnxruntime shadows the GPU one) - pull the clean docker7-<backend> image.
7. api_token: warn if no token is set - use API_TOKEN=disable for a trusted LAN, or the same token on both the plugin and the service.
8. model_smoke: runs a tiny inference on the loaded model; 'no model loaded yet' is fine on a fresh start, not an error.
Paste the /doctor output into a GitHub issue and we can pinpoint the problem in one reply.

entries.title: Anime4K mode (anime shader) - how to use it / it does nothing
entries.answer:
Anime4K is a real-time WebGL anime SHADER (Anime4K 4.0.1) - not a neural net, and it needs no server. As of v1.7.9 it actually runs; older builds loaded a dead CDN and silently fell back to plain sharpening. Step by step:
1. Update the plugin to v1.7.9 or newer.
2. In a WEB client (browser, not a native app) start an anime title.
3. Plugin settings -> Realtime Mode -> 'Anime4K (anime shader)' (or switch it in the in-player quick-menu), then play.
4. Confirm in the browser console (F12): success shows 'AI Upscaler RT: Anime4K (embedded, SIMPLE_M 2x) started'. In the Network tab, 'configurationpage?name=UPSCALERAnime4K' should return 200.
5. If your client lacks WebGL2 float textures, the console shows 'Anime4K unsupported ... using Lanczos' and it auto-falls back to the sharpen shader (no error, just not anime upscaling).
Notes: it runs client-side, so no Docker/GPU server is needed; it's best on anime/cartoon content. For live-action or guaranteed maximum quality, use Server AI or the batch scheduled task instead.

entries.title: Player button missing / "Could not inject player script" (read-only web root)
entries.answer:
The plugin adds the player button by writing one `<script>` tag into jellyfin-web's `index.html`. If the log shows `Cannot write to ... (read-only): Access to the path '.../index.html' is denied`, the Jellyfin service user has no write access to the web root (typical for the native Debian/Ubuntu package, where `/usr/share/jellyfin/web` is owned by root).

Fix (native package):
```
sudo chown jellyfin /usr/share/jellyfin/web/index.html
sudo systemctl restart jellyfin
```
Fix (Windows installer): Jellyfin runs as the NetworkService account by default, which cannot write to `Program Files`. In an administrator Command Prompt:
```
icacls "C:\Program Files\Jellyfin\Server\jellyfin-web\index.html" /grant *S-1-5-20:M
net stop JellyfinServer && net start JellyfinServer
```
Running the tray app instead of the service? Grant your own account: `/grant "%USERNAME%":M`, then restart the tray app.
After the restart the log says `Player script injected via <web folder>` and the button is permanent.

Notes:
- Visiting the plugin config page only activates the button for your **current browser tab** — after a refresh or on another device it is gone again. Only the index.html injection is permanent.
- A `jellyfin-web` package update replaces index.html (owner root again) — repeat the chown once if the warning returns; the plugin re-injects on the next restart.
- There is no "Upscale" button on item pages. Whole libraries are upscaled by the scheduled task **Scan & Upscale Library** (Dashboard → Scheduled Tasks).
- Official Docker image: web root is writable, works out of the box. Deliberately read-only containers: overlay a patched `index.html` via bind mount.

entries.title: Model download fails with "sha256 mismatch"
entries.answer:
Since v1.8.3.4 the AI service verifies a pinned sha256 checksum **before** activating a downloaded model (supply-chain guard). A `sha256 mismatch` error means the downloaded file does not match the catalog pin:
1. Usually a **corrupted/interrupted download** — just retry the download.
2. If it keeps failing, the **upstream file changed** (the hosting repo replaced the file). That is worth reporting: open a GitHub issue with the model id so the catalog pin gets updated.
The failed file is never activated — your existing models are unaffected.

entries.title: Does it work with Jellyfin 12?
entries.answer: v1.8.3.32 was the first native Jellyfin 12 / .NET 10 release; v1.8.3.33 is the current one (redesigned menus and the SDR/HDR fixes). It passed 443 C# tests against 12.0 and another 443 against 12.1. The 12.0-targeted publish loaded in an isolated official Jellyfin 12.1 container, injected its player script and reached Healthy startup. Actual playback, GPU, HDR and target-server acceptance remain unverified. v1.8.3.32 and all seven regular Docker variants are published. Version pins and latest/docker7 tags point to 1.8.3.32. See docs/RELEASE-PLAN-v1.8.3.32.md.

entries.title: Why are some models marked [self-host required]?
entries.answer:
Models marked **[self-host required]** have **no working public ONNX download** — community HuggingFace repos get deleted, some published exports are broken (fail to load in onnxruntime), and some models were only ever released as .pth weights. The catalog keeps them listed honestly instead of serving dead links.
- A 2026-07 health sweep checked every catalog URL: broken entries were either re-pointed to verified mirrors or marked self-host with the reason in the catalog entry.
- To use one anyway: export/convert the weights to ONNX yourself and drop the file into the service's model directory — see `docs/MODEL-HOSTING.md` in the repo.
- In most cases a listed alternative covers the same niche (e.g. `fallin-soft-x2` for anime real-time, `nomos8kdat-x4` for JPEG restoration).

entries.title: Importing community models (OpenModelDB) / use your own model
entries.answer:
Beyond the curated catalog, the **[Importable models](models-import.html)** page lists community models from [OpenModelDB](https://openmodeldb.info) that work with the plugin's ONNX pipeline:
- **~60 models are ready to use** - published as ONNX with a direct download URL and sha256 checksum (license shown per model, **NC = non-commercial**).
- **~600 more** exist only as PyTorch/NCNN weights and would need an ONNX export first.

**Easiest way (plugin v1.8.3.6+):** Jellyfin Dashboard → Plugins → AI Upscaler → card **Import Community Model** - pick the model; the plugin downloads it, verifies the pinned sha256 and registers it as `omdb-<id>` automatically (NC models warn before import). Since **v1.8.3.8** this covers the WHOLE catalog: zip-packed releases import one-click, the `:5000` dashboard has its own import section, a file-install form takes `.onnx` (direct) or `.pth` (auto-converted with the optional `docker7-converter` image, ~500 of the 609 convertible models), and imports land in the new **★ Favorites** card.

**Manual alternative** (the AI service has a custom-model upload API):
1. Download the ONNX file from the page (verify the sha256 shown).
2. Upload it to your AI service:
```
curl -X POST http://<service>:5000/models/upload \n  -F file=@model.onnx -F model_name=my-model-x4 -F scale=4
```
(add `-H "X-Api-Token: ..."` if your service uses a token; requires `ENABLE_MODEL_UPLOAD=true`, the default)
3. The service validates the model and registers it - it appears in the plugin's model list immediately. Remove it later via `DELETE /models/upload/{model_name}`.

Notes: imported models are **not curated or benchmarked**; check the license before commercial use (the page can filter out NC models); the page refreshes weekly from OpenModelDB.

entries.title: HDR videos: what's supported, and why an SDR video can be refused as HDR
keywords: hdr realtime and masking are not supported
entries.answer:
HDR works only as a **batch job** (library or scheduled task), and only for **PQ / ST.2084 with BT.2020 colours at 10-bit or more** (HDR10). Frames travel as 16-bit RGB PNGs and the output is 10-bit x265 with the static HDR metadata copied over. Refused on purpose, with an error instead of a silent SDR fallback: **HLG**, **Dolby Vision / HDR10+** (dynamic metadata), **real-time HDR** and **multi-frame models on HDR**.

**Fixed in v1.8.3.33:** v1.8.3.31–v1.8.3.32 refused some *SDR* videos with an HDR message: DVD/SD rips tagged `smpte170m`/`bt470bg` in real time, and 10-bit files without colour tags in real time and in library jobs. v1.8.3.33 also keeps the model's detail in HDR output. Staying on v1.8.3.31 (Jellyfin 10.11)? Upscale SD rips with a library job; for untagged HD 10-bit MKV files you can add the SDR tags without re-encoding, then refresh the item's metadata in Jellyfin: `mkvpropedit "file.mkv" --edit track:v1 --set colour-transfer-characteristics=1 --set colour-primaries=1 --set colour-matrix-coefficients=1`

HDR output quality has not been verified on real HDR hardware yet.

entries.title: Real-time says "Busy", HTTP 503/429 or "Circuit breaker open" / stops after 10 frames
entries.answer:
**Stops after 10 frames / "Rate limit exceeded. Max 10 upscale requests per minute"** was issue #79: live frames counted against the limit meant for image actions. **Fixed in v1.8.3.31**, so update the plugin (Jellyfin 10.11: v1.8.3.31, Jellyfin 12: v1.8.3.32). The 10-per-minute limit still applies to explicit image actions such as Compare and Upscale image.

What the other messages mean:
1. **HTTP 503 "Busy"**: the AI service is already processing as many frames as it allows. The player waits (250 ms up to 2 s, or whatever the service's `Retry-After` asks) and then sends a fresh frame. An occasional 503 on a loaded server is normal.
2. **"Circuit breaker open"**: several requests in a row failed, so the service pauses briefly. The container log (`docker logs <container>`) shows the real error; often the GPU ran out of memory or no model is loaded.
3. **Constant 503s**: the server can't keep up. Use a lighter model (e.g. `span-x2`, `clearreality-x4`), lower the real-time capture width (Settings → Real-Time Upscaling), or let **Auto** decide: it only picks Server AI when the benchmark reaches 80 % of the video's frame rate.

**Fixed in v1.8.3.33:** during an outage the stale frame is hidden after 1.5 s instead of freezing over the video, and a server that delivers under half the video's frame rate for 5 s hands over to Lanczos. On v1.8.3.31–v1.8.3.32, stop real-time upscaling or switch the mode in the AI Upscaler menu (**Realtime** tab).

entries.title: Cover animals or objects during playback (object masking)
entries.answer:
Object masking covers detected objects, for example animals, with a box or a blur during playback. It was built for discussion #11.
1. **Import a detection model first.** None ships with the plugin; `tiny-yolov3-11.onnx` from the ONNX model zoo works. Use the import on the settings page's **Models** tab.
2. Settings page → **Models** → **Object Masking**: enter the model id, the classes (COCO names such as `dog,cat`, or `animals` for the whole group), box or blur, and padding. Then **Load Detection Model**.
3. Switch it on from the player menu: **Auto** tab → **Cover objects**.

While it runs it **replaces** real-time upscaling on that stream, because two inference passes per frame don't keep up with playback. It works on SDR video only.

entries.title: Face restoration (GFPGAN / CodeFormer)
entries.answer:
Face restoration sharpens heavily degraded faces in old or low-quality video: faces are detected, cropped to 512×512, restored with GFPGAN or CodeFormer and blended back.
1. Settings page → **Models** → **AI Face Restoration**: pick a model, then **Load Face Model**.
2. Turn it on with **Enable Face Restoration** there, or from the player menu (**Auto** tab → **Face restoration**).
3. **Preview on Selected Media** shows the effect before you start a long job.

It costs extra time on every frame, so it suits batch jobs on old sources better than live playback on a slow server.

entries.title: Video filters and looks (Cinematic, Vivid, Noir …)
entries.answer:
Filters change the look of the video without transcoding.
1. During playback open the AI Upscaler menu → **Filters**: pick a preset (Cinematic, Vivid, Noir, Teal/Orange …) or use the Brightness / Contrast / Saturation sliders. These apply instantly in your browser.
2. **Advanced** (gamma, sharpness, colour temperature, vignette, grain, denoise) is applied by the server and takes effect on the next seek.
3. **Save** makes the look the default and needs an admin account. The settings page has the same controls on its **Filters** tab.

In Auto mode the plugin may *suggest* a look for a video, but it never replaces your chosen preset by itself.
